title: Book 2 — Euterpe, Chapter 254
paragraphs: In this way, then, the beast is tested; and their appointed manner of sacrifice is as follows. They lead the sealed beast to the altar where they are performing the sacrifice, and then kindle a fire. After that, having poured libations of wine over the altar so that it runs down upon the victim, and having called upon the god, they cut its throat; and having cut its throat they sever the head from the body. The body of the beast they flay, but upon the head they first utter many imprecations; and then those who have a market and Hellenes sojourning among them for trade carry it to the market-place and sell it, while those who have no Hellenes among them cast it into the river. This is the form of imprecation they utter over the heads, praying that if any evil is about to fall either upon those sacrificing or upon the land of Egypt in general, it may come rather upon this head. Now as regards the heads of sacrificed beasts and the pouring of wine over them, all the Egyptians have the same customs equally for all their sacrifices; and for this reason no Egyptian will eat of the head either of this or of any other kind of animal.
